title: Savoy Man Dies Three Days After His Wife
text:
Savoy Man Dies Three Days After His Wife

(Herald News Service)

SAVOY—Funeral services for C. H. Booth, 79, were held at 3:30 p.m. today just two days after the burial of his wife on Tuesday. He died Wednesday at 9:15 p.m. at his home in Savoy from a heart ailment. Interment was at Sunnyside Cemetery with Earnheart-Strickland in charge.

Robert D. Bankes, minister of a Sherman Church of Christ, Ralph Edmonson, minister of the Savoy Church of Christ, and the Rev. Baxter Bryant, pastor of the Bells Methodist Church, officiated. Pallbearers were E. L. McCollum, R. W. Wrenn, Earl Blakey, Ralph Duncan, O. L. Baker and W. H. Blount.

Booth was born Nov. 26. 1870, in Virginia. On Oct. 21, 1894, he married Miss Sarah Jane Hanna in Denison. He was a farmer and had been in the trucking business. He was a member of the Savoy Church of Christ.

Mrs. Booth had been in ill health for some time and died at 6:30 a.m. Monday.

Survivors include three sons, Roy Booth of Waco, Ray Booth of Bells and E. H. Booth, Jr., of Savoy; three daughters Mrs. Carl Orndorff of Savoy, Mrs. Dan Sweeney of Savoy and Mrs. Roy Stephens of Sherman; two brothers, W. F. Booth and Jim Booth, both of Virginia; six grandchildren, and three great-grandchildren.
